label: Stock accuracy gain
definition: Perceived gain in the accuracy of stock records, measured or expected, that the technology brings to the unit.
example: INT-01: counts moved from about seventy to about ninety-six percent on tagged lines.

label: Tag and reader cost
definition: Investment and running cost of tags, readers and handhelds, and the payback that the unit expects from them.
example: INT-01: readers and handhelds cost more than the tags; the payback needed a supplier contribution.

label: Integration effort
definition: Effort to connect the tag events to the existing information system, including interfaces written by the vendor.
example: INT-01: the ERP needed a vendor-written interface.
reason: Not in the literature codebook; named by the respondent as the hardest part.

label: Lack of in-house skills
definition: Absence of people who can run the technology, or dependence on a single person who holds the knowledge.
example: INT-01: one person knew both the warehouse and the database and his departure cost months.

label: Board sponsorship
definition: Support or conviction of the management board, triggered by the evidence presented to it.
example: INT-01: the pilot numbers convinced the board.

label: Change of receiving process
definition: Change of routines at the receiving dock or in the warehouse, and the confusion that accompanies it.
example: INT-01: receiving staff had to learn reader zones and a gate-based routine.
reason: Named in the field: a process change that the literature codebook does not describe.

label: Supplier tagging requirement
definition: Requirement or condition imposed by a supplier to tag goods at source, or the fact that the supplier already does so.
example: INT-01: the largest supplier made tagging a condition of the next contract.
reason: Environmental pressure from a supplier, separate from customer demand.

label: Customer traceability demand
definition: Expectation of customers, including project buyers, that orders can be traced to the item.
example: INT-01: two project customers asked for traceability that was not yet in their contracts.

label: Sector standard
definition: Lack of a shared standard for labels, tag content or placement, or the wish for one.
example: INT-01: readers do not handle cartons and pallets tagged differently.

label: Privacy concern about tags
definition: Worry that tags can be read outside the premises or by customers after the sale, and the measures taken in response.
example: INT-01: staff asked about reading from outside the building; tags were deactivated at the till.
reason: Not attached to a TOE context: a concern about the use of the tags that the framework does not name.
